intro: This is a mantra from the **Yajurveda** (Yajurveda, Taittiriya Samhita 4.5.1, Sri Rudram). Below are the Sanskrit text and a **plain English meaning**.
takeaways: Source: Yajurveda, Taittiriya Samhita 4.5.1, Sri Rudram.
The four Vedas are Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda and Atharvaveda.
Vedic mantras are learned by listening and repeating.

p: **नमस्ते रुद्र मन्यव उतो त इषवे नमः । नमस्ते अस्तु धन्वने बाहुभ्यामुत ते नमः ॥**
Salutations to your fury, Rudra, to your arrow, to your bow, and to your arms.
The Yajurveda is one of the four Vedas, the oldest scriptures of Sanatana Dharma, handed down by voice for thousands of years.

faq.a: Salutations to your fury, Rudra, to your arrow, to your bow, and to your arms.
There are **four**: Rig, Yajur, Sama and Atharva.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering.
